subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Charm Pricing: The Power of 9
description: A quick win: understand Charm Pricing: The Power of 9.

hook.text: A shirt priced at $39 outsold the same shirt at $34. The nine ending made it feel like a better deal. Logic lost.

buildup.text: Charm pricing uses prices ending in 9 or 99. Anderson and Simester proved it increases sales even against lower prices.

discovery.text: The brain reads left to right. $3.99 registers as three dollars, not four.

twist.text: Luxury brands avoid nines. Round prices like $200 signal quality. Nines signal bargains. The ending tells a story.

climax.text: Next time you see a .99 price, mentally round up. The real price is the next dollar.

punchline.text: $9.99 is not nine dollars. It is ten in disguise.

quiz.question: Why does charm pricing work?
options: The left digit anchors perception, making the price seem lower
Odd numbers are inherently more attractive
